quick.summary: Why splitting storage and compute prepares you for growth.
quick.takeaway: Separate your storage and processor so they can scale safely.

beats.line: I put the database and the processor on one machine. Why change it?
Imagine buying a machine that washes and dries your clothes in one drum.
Until the dryer breaks. Then you cannot wash anything either.
Can I just say tightly coupled?
That works. Tightly coupled means one failure takes down everything.
In two years, your data will be huge.
Keep storage separate from the processor. They can grow at different speeds.
So I split them up. If the processor fails, the data is safe.
And you can easily swap the broken part.

quiz.question: What is the main advantage of separating storage from compute?
options: They can be upgraded or replaced independently without taking down the other.
It combines all costs into a single billing cycle.
It completely eliminates the risk of network delays.
It allows the database to process math faster.
quiz.explanation: Decoupling systems means a failure or heavy load in one area does not break the other.

quiz.question: A tightly coupled system is usually the most future-proof design.
quiz.explanation: Tightly coupled systems break down easily as load increases. It is better to build modular, separate systems.
